sections.extract: We review the basic notions and results about the sign--determined Reidemeister torsion introduced by V. Turaev which are needed in this paper. Details can be found in Milnor's survey~\cite{Milnor:1966} and in Turaev's monograph~\cite{Turaev:2002}.

sections.title: A derivative formula
sections.extract: \label{section:derform} We prove a relation between the polynomial torsion and the non--abelian Reidemeister torsion. More precisely, we prove that the non--abelian Reidemeister is a sort of ``differential coefficient'' associated to the polynomial torsion. We review the definition of the non--abelian Reidemeister torsion (for more details, we refer to~\cite[Chap.~3]{Porti:1997}).

sections.title: Reciprocality of the polynomial torsion (with sign)
Reciprocality properties
sections.extract: The Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K(t)$ of a knot $K \subset S^3$ is known to be reciprocal in the sense that $\Delta_K(t^{-1}) = \pm t^s \Delta_K(t)$ from a long time. This property was first observed by Seifert~\cite{Seifert:1934} and is a consequence of Poincar\'e duality. Milnor~\cite{Milnor:1962} proved it again using the interpretation of the Alexander polynomial as an abelian Reidemeister torsion.
